root.name: Semi-Slav Defense: Semi-Meran Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 d5 2. c4 c6 3. Nc3 Nf6 4. e3 e6 5. Nf3 Nbd7 6. Bd3 dxc4 7. Bxc4

overview: After 6.Bd3 dxc4 7.Bxc4, Black usually plays ...b5, then ...Bb7, ...a6 and ...c5 in the Meran fashion. White aims for e4 and e5, with Bd3, O-O and Qe2; Black's queenside expansion gives counterplay. Both sides have long theoretical lines and the central break e4-e5 or ...c5 leads to sharp tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Play Bd3, O-O and e4 to drive back the knights
Push e5 to attack the f6 knight
Attack the b5 pawn with a4 or Nxb5 tactics

black_ideas.idea: Use the queenside majority and the bishops

typical_structures.structure: Meran structure with Black ...b5/...c5 queenside pawns against a White e4 centre
Open lines after ...c5 and exchanges in the centre

character.notes: The e4-e5 and ...c5 breaks lead to forcing lines where one wrong move can lose fast.

gambit.notes: The c4 pawn is returned at once; nothing is sacrificed.

soundness.notes: The Meran is one of the most respected Black systems.

structure.notes: Black's ...c5 break leaves a half-open file, and the centre is partly open.

approach.notes: A main-line system played by top players.

level.notes: Long forcing lines in the Meran must be known, as well as understanding the plans.
